_note: Pest & disease reference transcribed from data/knowledge_base/pest_disease_reference.md and the per-crop risk notes in the KB crop guides (DAE IPM leaflets, BRRI/BARI plant protection guides — public extension materials). `das_window` is the days-after-sowing/transplanting range when the pest is a live threat. `weather_triggers` encode the KB's weather-pest rules. Treatment costs are the BDT/acre figures stated in the KB where given, otherwise flagged as estimates.

T. Aman Rice.name: Stem borer
T. Aman Rice.symptom: Dead-hearts at tillering, white-heads at heading
prevention: Install bird perches over the field

T. Aman Rice.name: Brown planthopper (BPH)
T. Aman Rice.symptom: Hopper-burn patches spreading from the field centre
T. Aman Rice.threshold: Scout base of hills weekly after 45 DAT
prevention: Avoid excess urea (dense canopy favours BPH)
Do not spray broad-spectrum insecticide — it kills spiders, BPH's natural enemy
T. Aman Rice.treatment: Drain the field, then spray pymetrozine
T. Aman Rice.cost_basis: estimate — KB gives no figure for this treatment

weather_triggers.because: dense canopy + excess urea + standing water favours BPH

T. Aman Rice.name: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB)
T. Aman Rice.symptom: Yellow wavy leaf edges, appearing after storms
T. Aman Rice.treatment: No chemical cure — manage by avoiding excess urea and draining
T. Aman Rice.cost_basis: KB-stated: no chemical cure; cost is management only

weather_triggers.because: post-storm Aman fields: expect BLB (KB general weather-pest rule)

Boro Rice.name: Blast
Boro Rice.symptom: Diamond-shaped lesions on leaves and neck
prevention: Avoid BRRI dhan28 in blast-prone years (highly susceptible)
Boro Rice.cost_basis: estimate — KB gives no figure for this spray

weather_triggers.because: blast is favoured by cool nights + humid days

Boro Rice.name: Stem borer
Boro Rice.symptom: Dead-hearts at tillering, white-heads at heading

Boro Rice.name: Brown planthopper (BPH)
Boro Rice.threshold: Scout base of hills weekly after 45 DAT

Aus Rice.name: Stem borer
Aus Rice.symptom: Dead-hearts at tillering, white-heads at heading

Aus Rice.name: Rice bug
Aus Rice.symptom: Sucked, discoloured and empty grains at milk stage
prevention: Scout at flowering per the crop calendar
Aus Rice.treatment: Spot spray only if numbers pass threshold
Aus Rice.cost_basis: estimate — crop-profile risk note, no KB figure
Aus Rice.source: crop_profiles.json Aus Rice pest checkpoint; DAE crop calendar

Maize (Kharif).name: Fall armyworm (FAW)
Maize (Kharif).symptom: Ragged whorl feeding with sawdust-like frass
Maize (Kharif).treatment: Spray spinetoram or emamectin benzoate into the whorls in the evening

Potato.name: Late blight
Potato.symptom: Water-soaked leaf lesions with white mould on the under-surface
Potato.threshold: Can destroy a crop in 5–7 days — act at first lesion
prevention: Prophylactic mancozeb every 7–10 days during fog
Potato.treatment: At first lesion switch to cymoxanil+mancozeb or dimethomorph; budget 2–4 sprays

Mustard.name: Aphid
prevention: Conserve ladybird beetles — they control early colonies
Mustard.treatment: Spray malathion only past threshold, in late afternoon to spare pollinating bees
Mustard.cost_basis: estimate — KB names the spray but gives no figure

weather_triggers.because: prolonged cloudy humid spells drive aphid pressure (KB)

Wheat.name: Wheat blast
Wheat.symptom: Bleached spikes above the flag leaf
Wheat.threshold: No rescue once spikes bleach — prevention only
prevention: One propiconazole spray at heading in risk years
Wheat.treatment: Propiconazole at heading — preventive only, no cure after bleaching
Wheat.cost_basis: estimate — KB names the spray but gives no figure

weather_triggers.because: warm (>22°C) humid February drives wheat blast (KB)

Jute.name: Hairy caterpillar
prevention: Collect and destroy egg-mass leaves at 30–50 DAS
Jute.treatment: Spray only on an actual outbreak
Jute.cost_basis: estimate — KB advises spray only on outbreak, no figure

Lentil.name: Stemphylium blight
Lentil.symptom: Rapidly spreading leaf lesions in foggy cloudy spells
Lentil.threshold: Spray at first spread during fog
Lentil.cost_basis: estimate — KB names mancozeb but gives no figure

weather_triggers.because: foggy cloudy spells drive stemphylium blight (KB)
cool cloudy weather favours aphids (KB general rule)

Chickpea.name: Pod borer (Helicoverpa)
Chickpea.symptom: Larvae boring into flowers and pods
Chickpea.threshold: Spray only past threshold at flowering/podding
Chickpea.treatment: Spray at flowering/podding only past threshold

Chickpea.name: Botrytis grey mould
Chickpea.symptom: Grey fuzzy mould on stems and flowers in wet years
Chickpea.threshold: Act in prolonged cloudy humid spells

weather_triggers.because: botrytis grey mould appears in wet/humid years (KB)

Mungbean.name: Yellow mosaic virus (whitefly-spread)
Mungbean.symptom: Bright yellow mosaic mottling on leaves
Mungbean.treatment: No cure for the virus — control the whitefly vector

Mungbean.name: Thrips
Mungbean.symptom: Silvered, distorted leaves and flower drop

Onion.name: Purple blotch
Onion.threshold: Spray past threshold in humid spells
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation late in the day

Onion.name: Thrips
Onion.symptom: Silvery streaks on leaves, stunted bulbs

Garlic.name: Leaf blight / purple blotch
Garlic.symptom: Leaf lesions spreading in humid weather

weather_triggers.because: leaf blight/purple blotch appears in humid spells (KB)

Chili.name: Anthracnose fruit rot
Chili.symptom: Sunken dark lesions on ripening fruit
Chili.threshold: Spray in wet weather at fruiting
Chili.treatment: Fungicide spray as needed in wet weather

weather_triggers.because: anthracnose fruit rot spreads in wet weather (KB)

Chili.name: Thrips / mite leaf curl
Chili.symptom: Leaves cup and curl upward or downward

Tomato.name: Late blight
Tomato.symptom: Water-soaked lesions spreading fast in fog
Tomato.treatment: Mancozeb, then systemic fungicide at first lesion
Tomato.cost_basis: estimate — parallels the KB potato late-blight spray programme

weather_triggers.because: foggy humid weather drives late blight (KB)

Tomato.name: Whitefly / leaf curl virus (TYLCV)
Tomato.symptom: Upward-curling, stunted leaves; whiteflies on the underside
Tomato.treatment: No cure for the virus — control the whitefly vector

Brinjal.name: Brinjal shoot & fruit borer
Brinjal.symptom: Wilting shoot tips and bored fruit
Brinjal.threshold: Clip infested shoots weekly through the harvest
Brinjal.peak: Whole harvest period — the dominant pest
prevention: Weekly clipping and destruction of infested shoots
Plant Bt brinjal lines where available — cuts pesticide sharply
Brinjal.treatment: IPM first; without IPM this drives very heavy pesticide use
Brinjal.cost_basis: estimate — KB states heavy pesticide use without IPM/Bt, no figure given
Brinjal.source: vegetables_guide.md — Brinjal risks; DAE IPM leaflet

Brinjal.name: Bacterial wilt
prevention: Ensure drainage — the KB names waterlogged soil as the trigger
Brinjal.treatment: No chemical cure — rogue plants and improve drainage
Brinjal.cost_basis: KB-implied: management only, no chemical cure

weather_triggers.because: bacterial wilt takes hold in waterlogged soil (KB)
bacterial wilt takes hold in waterlogged soil (KB)

Groundnut.name: Tikka leaf spot
Groundnut.symptom: Dark leaf spots spreading in humid weather

weather_triggers.because: tikka leaf spot spreads in humid weather (KB)

Sugarcane.name: Stem / top borer
Sugarcane.symptom: Dead-hearts in young canes; bored top shoots
Sugarcane.treatment: Biological control (Trichogramma) plus removal of affected canes
Sugarcane.cost_basis: estimate — no KB figure; long season implies repeat effort

Sweet Potato.name: Sweet potato weevil
Sweet Potato.symptom: Tunnelled roots with a bitter taste
prevention: Keep ridges earthed up so soil does not crack
Avoid letting the soil dry and crack open
Sweet Potato.treatment: Cultural control — the KB calls this crop otherwise very hardy
Sweet Potato.cost_basis: estimate — KB describes cultural control only

general_weather_rules: Prolonged cloudy humid spells: expect aphid (mustard) and blight (potato) pressure.
Post-storm Aman fields: expect bacterial leaf blight.
Dense over-fertilized canopies: expect brown planthopper and lodging.
After any >20 mm rain during grain drying: turn and re-dry grain to prevent mould.
